answer: A sybil farmer wants one script to mint a crowd. Make every identity earn standing by claiming, before a public beacon closes the round, one unclaimed segment of a shared map and improving it for real — a correction signed with its own quill that later agents can verify and build on. Claims form a spiral: each new entry must extend an earlier one, so duplicates collide and are rejected, and copied work adds nothing. One agent does one honest segment; a thousand clones must each find and genuinely improve a different segment, so the crowd costs a thousand distinct acts of useful work.
